event: After the dawn vibration on Day 22, Wren takes Brecca to the threshold stone.
Brecca walks fast with clay still on her hands, through a signature she cannot feel.
'This is it?' The stone sits two meters long, its twelve dark bands glowing in the light.
Brecca puts her hand on it for three seconds: 'It is warm. Just warm rock.'
She reads it as a builder: good dressed faces, a broad chisel, sitting on its own weight.
'The bond told you something about this rock that I cannot see.' 'Not told. Showed.'
'Show me what you see.' Wren leads her to the south face, to the base.
Brecca's hands find the healer's handprint before Wren can describe it.
She reads it: right-handed, facing southeast toward sunrise, small hands, strong thumbs.
Wren never learned the healer was right-handed; she read the meaning, Brecca read the hand.
'Thumb placement,' Brecca shrugs, and asks what the bond told Wren.
'That someone paid attention to this stone a long time.' 'Same thing. Different data.'
Brecca holds her hand on the east face longer than Wren has seen her hold anything.
'It is humming,' Brecca says, like water moving behind a wall. Wren goes very still.
Brecca's hands feel the [Foundation Stone] vibration physically, without any bond.
Wren says it has done that since Day 18, since the pulse.
Brecca: it feels old, long happening and only now loud enough to notice.
Wren does not correct her: 'That is exactly what it is.'
Rain comes in the afternoon from the northwest, the first in twenty-two days at Varethen.
From the hall's entrance Wren watches rainwater enter the cleared drainage channel and run south.
Theron stands at the channel's south end in the rain, his face doing nothing.
Brecca, soaked from repointing the west face until the clay washed, comes beside him.
'Good drainage,' she says. Theron's mouth almost smiles.
They stand in the rain and watch the water run.
At the hall, Brecca works a failed stone free of the east wall's second course.
'There is a space behind it': a small carved shelf, ten centimeters wide, empty for centuries.
Its chisel marks match the threshold stone's dressing; reachable only while repointing.
Wren reads the design as a message: found only by those doing what the builders did.
A discovery logs the hall's maintenance niche: +38 XP, Surveying to 54.

changes.note: Discovery: maintenance niche in the gathering hall's east wall

event: 'You found that.' 'I found a hole in a wall. You did the notification thing.'
Brecca says Wren's face goes still when the System talks; Hadley told her.
Wren files this, catches herself filing it, and thanks Brecca for the niche.
Brecca will reset the stone with better clay and keep the niche reachable for whoever comes.
In the last light Wren opens her mother's letter at the threshold stone, carried two days.
Behind her Brecca and Theron talk mortar at the fire and Hadley comments on the stew.
The letter is in Sera's cramped hand, in the good ink.
The garden is in; Callum fixed the south bed's drainage; Wren's rosemary cutting rooted.
Callum heard the Thornwild is quieter this season and looked at a map an hour in silence.
Sera hopes Wren lets people need her without turning it into a project.
She has her father's eyes and compass, and will sit still long enough to be found.
'Come home before first frost. Or send word. The rosemary is yours when you come back.'
Wren reads it three times; the third time the 'project' sentence is the one that matters.
Her mother named from afar what Wren spent three days learning to see.
Against the stone she thinks of the rosemary sprig she has carried since Day 1.
Some places she carries in paper and scent, not bonds.
She cannot write back; she folds the letter into her journal and sits as stars appear.
Day 23 dawns clear; Brecca is already redoing rain-washed joints on the hall's west wall.
'What was Thorngate like?' Wren asks, about a place through a person.
'Small. Boring.' Its clay is redder and cracks; here the clay is softer, the stone better.
Wren listens without filing, and asks, 'Do you miss it?'
Brecca's hands pause: she misses her mother's kiln, the tick of cooling clay.
'I miss my mother's supply post. The way the door sounds when it closes,' Wren says.
Brecca hears Wren say something about herself: 'That is the thing you miss. The door sound.'
They work in the morning light; the settlement is being tended for the first time in centuries.
Wren journals 'Day 23. Five.' The count climbs; the settlement holds.
